cves.summary: Cross-site scripting vulnerability in analog before 5.22 allows remote attackers to execute Javascript via an HTTP request containing the script, which is entered into a web logfile and not properly filtered by analog during display.

Imlib before 1.9.13 sometimes uses the NetPBM package to load trusted images, which could allow attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via certain weaknesses of NetPBM.
Kebi WebMail allows remote attackers to access the administrator menu and gain privileges via the /a/ hidden directory, which is installed under the web document root.

wrshdsp.exe in Denicomp Winsock RSHD/NT 2.21.00 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption) via (1) in 2.20.00 and earlier, an invalid port number such as a negative number, which causes a connection attempt to that port and all ports below 1024, and (2) in 2.21.00, a port number of 1024.
Some AIO operations in FreeBSD 4.4 may be delayed until after a call to execve, which could allow a local user to overwrite memory of the new process and gain privileges.
Untrusted search path vulnerability in day5datacopier in SGI IRIX 6.2 allows local users to execute arbitrary commands via a modified PATH environment variable that points to a malicious cp program.
Buffer overflow in chkey in Solaris 2.5.1 and earlier allows local users to gain root privileges via a long command line argument.
Buffer overflow in AIX lquerylv program gives root access to local users.
Vulnerability in runtime linker program rld in SGI IRIX 6.x and earlier allows local users to gain privileges via setuid and setgid programs.

The Visual Form Builder WordPress plugin through 3.1 does not perform authorization or nonce checks when reordering form fields, allowing any authenticated user (Subscriber and above) to alter the field structure of any form on the site, persistently breaking its public rendering.

A flaw has been found in Freedesktop Poppler 26.07.0. Impacted is the function JBIG2Stream::rewind of the file poppler/JBIG2Stream.cc. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 26.08.0 is recommended to address this issue. Patch name: 5e49250f13b0390edeb3f90eb4c02c9941f97067. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

A vulnerability was detected in Freedesktop Poppler 26.07.0. This issue affects the function SampledFunction::SampledFunction of the file poppler/Function.cc of the component SampledFunction. The manipulation of the argument BitsPerSample results in integer overflow. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is now public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through a bug report but has not responded yet.

Apache before 1.3.20 on Windows and OS/2 systems allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (GPF) via an HTTP request for a URI that contains a large number of / (slash) or other characters, which causes certain functions to dereference a null pointer.

Buffer overflow in MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) 1.2.2 and earlier allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code via base-64 encoded data, which is not properly handled when the radix_encode function processes file glob output from the ftpglob function.
Computer Associates ARCserveIT 6.61 and 6.63 (also called ARCservIT) allows local users to overwrite arbitrary files via a symlink attack on the temporary files (1) asagent.tmp or (2) inetd.tmp.
Beck IPC GmbH IPC@CHIP Embedded-Webserver allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long HTTP request.
Buffer overflow in CDE Print Viewer (dtprintinfo) allows local users to execute arbitrary code by copying text from the clipboard into the Help window.
Beck IPC GmbH IPC@CHIP Embedded-Webserver allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via a webserver root directory set to system root.
Batch files in the Oracle web listener ows-bin directory allow remote attackers to execute commands via a malformed URL that includes '?&'.
Buffer overflow in POP3 and IMAP servers in the MERCUR mail server suite allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service.
SuSE Linux IMAP server allows remote attackers to bypass IMAP authentication and gain privileges.
Buffer overflow in the MERCUR WebView WebMail server allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long mail_user parameter in the GET request.
Buffer overflow in Fastream FTP++ 2.0 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary commands via a long username.
Htgrep CGI program allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files by specifying the full pathname in the hdr parameter.
XFree86 startx command is vulnerable to a symlink attack, allowing local users to create files in restricted directories, possibly allowing them to gain privileges or cause a denial of service.
Local users can gain privileges using the debug utility in the MPE/iX operating system.

Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Infopop Ultimate Bulletin Board (UBB) 6.x allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary web script and gain administrative access via the "displayed name" attribute of the "ubber" cookie.

admin.php in Digi-news 1.1 allows remote attackers to bypass authentication via a cookie with the username set to the name of the administrator, which satisfies an improper condition in admin.php that does not require a correct password.

MS Analysis module 2.0 for PHP-Nuke allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information via a direct request to (1) browsers.php, (2) mstrack.php, or (3) title.php, which reveal the full path in a PHP error message.

## Impact

With the default `router.options.sensitive: false`, Nuxt's page router resolves routes case-insensitively, so `/Admin` renders the same page as `/admin`. On the server, however, route rules were resolved with Nitro's route-rule matcher, which matches keys case-sensitively. A request whose path differs from a rule key only in letter case therefore rendered the page with none of that rule applied.

Earlier fixes ([GHSA-mm7m-92g8-7m47](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/security/advisories/GHSA-mm7m-92g8-7m47), [GHSA-hxvh-4h3w-prp9](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/security/advisories/GHSA-hxvh-4h3w-prp9)) case-folded the route rules that the Nuxt app itself reads, such as `appMiddleware`. This advisory covers the rules applied on the server:

- `redirect`: a rule used to send visitors away from a page, such as `'/admin/**': { redirect: '/login' }`, was skipped, and the page and its server-fetched data were rendered instead.
- `headers`: per-route response headers, including security headers such as `Content-Security-Policy` or `X-Frame-Options`, were not sent.
- `proxy`: the request was not proxied.
- `ssr: false` and `noScripts`: the page was server-rendered, or shipped scripts, despite the rule.
- `getRouteRules(event)` (auto-imported, or from `nuxt/server`) and `matchRouteRules` from `nuxt/server` returned no rules for the case variant.

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  routeRules: {
    '/admin/**': { redirect: '/login' },
  },
})
```

With this configuration, `/admin/secret` redirects to `/login`, but `/Admin/secret` rendered `app/pages/admin/secret.vue`.

## Mitigating factors

- Applications that set `router.options.sensitive: true` in `nuxt.config` are not affected, because their pages are only served for the exact case of the route.
- Access checks performed in server middleware, route middleware attached with `definePageMeta`, or in the page's data fetching are not affected. The issue only affects protections that rely on a server-side route rule matching the request path.

## Affected versions

`nuxt` `<4.6.2`, including all Nuxt 3 releases, and `@nuxt/nitro-server` `<4.6.2`.

## Patches

Fixed in `nuxt@4.6.2`. Nuxt 3 reached end of life on 31 July 2026 and will not receive a fix.

Nuxt now resolves server-side route rules itself, decoding and case-folding both the rule keys and the request path unless `router.options.sensitive` is set, and applies the result to Nitro's `redirect`, `headers` and `proxy` handling, the renderer, and the `getRouteRules` / `matchRouteRules` helpers.

When routing is case-insensitive, patched releases change some behaviour:

- Route rules also apply to case variants of server API routes. For example, `/API/x` now matches a `/api/**` `proxy` or `headers` rule.
- Rule keys that differ only in letter case now resolve to the same path on the server, and the later key takes precedence.

The following are not changed by this fix:

- `cache` and `swr` response caching is attached to server routes by Nitro's router, which matches case-sensitively. A case variant is still rendered with its route rules applied, but its response is not cached.
- Rules that a deployment preset compiles into platform configuration (for example Vercel's `config.json` or Netlify's `_redirects` and `_headers`) are matched by the platform. Once a request reaches the Nuxt server, the rules are applied as described above.
- If `sensitive` is set only in `app/router.options.ts`, the server follows the `nuxt.config` value. In that configuration route rules can only apply to more paths, never fewer.

## Workarounds

Upgrade to `nuxt@4.6.2`. If you cannot upgrade, including on Nuxt 3:

1. Set `router: { options: { sensitive: true } }` in `nuxt.config`, so pages are only served for the exact case of their route.
2. Alternatively, enforce access control in server middleware or route middleware rather than relying on a `redirect` route rule, and set security headers for every response rather than per route.

## Impact

`useHeadSafe` restricts head input to an allowlist of safe tags and attributes. For example, `bodyAttrs` is limited to `class` and `style`, event handler attributes are removed, and `<script>` tags are only kept for JSON types.

When `useHeadSafe` is called inside a server island (a `.server.vue` component or page, or a component rendered with `<NuxtIsland>`), the island renderer serialises the raw input of every head entry into the island response without the option that marks it as safe input. `<NuxtIsland>` then pushes that input into the page's head as a regular entry, both during server rendering and when hydrating or refetching on the client.

As a result, input that `useHeadSafe` would normally strip (such as `bodyAttrs.onload` or executable `<script>` content) is rendered into the page. If an application passes user-controlled data to `useHeadSafe` inside a server island, an attacker who controls that data can achieve stored cross-site scripting on the application's origin.

```vue
<!-- components/AuthorMeta.server.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const { data: author } = await useFetch('/api/author')
// author.value.head is user-authored, e.g. { bodyAttrs: { onload: '...' } }
useHeadSafe(author.value.head)
</script>
```

## Mitigating factors

- Server components are experimental. They are only active when the application defines a `.server.vue` component or page, or enables `experimental.componentIslands` and renders `<NuxtIsland>`.
- Exploitation requires the application to pass attacker-controlled data to `useHeadSafe` inside a server island. `useHeadSafe` called from regular (non-island) components and pages is not affected.

## Affected versions

`nuxt` `>=3.13.0`, when head support for server islands was introduced. Nuxt 2 is not affected.

## Patches

Fixed in `nuxt@4.6.2`. Nuxt 3 reached end of life on 31 July 2026 and will not receive a fix.

Patched releases apply Unhead's safe input filtering to `useHeadSafe` entries on the server before they are added to the island response, so `islandResponse.head` (including what `render:island` hooks see) only contains input that `useHeadSafe` allows.

## Workarounds

Upgrade to `nuxt@4.6.2`. If you cannot upgrade, including on Nuxt 3:

1. Call `useHeadSafe` with untrusted input from a regular component or page rather than from inside a server island.
2. Alternatively, validate untrusted head input against your own allowlist before passing it to `useHeadSafe` inside a server island.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

cves.summary:
## Impact

An application that renders `<NuxtLink :to="...">` with a value it does not control can be made to render an anchor whose `href` executes script in the application's origin when clicked.

This is an incomplete fix for [GHSA-934w-87qh-qr26](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/security/advisories/GHSA-934w-87qh-qr26) (CVE-2026-53722). It only affects applications running without a `pages/` directory, where `pages` resolves to `false` and Nuxt registers its own router in place of vue-router. Applications using vue-router are not affected.

Prefixing `javascript:` with an ASCII C0 control character, for example `%01`, meant the value was not recognised as having a protocol. It was classified as an internal route and so never reached the protocol check added in GHSA-934w-87qh-qr26, and the router used for `pages: false` passed it through to the rendered `href` unchanged. Browsers strip the leading control character and run the result as a script URL.

Both `<NuxtLink custom>` and the default anchor are affected, and the `href` is present in the server-rendered HTML.

## Mitigating factors

- The application must have `pages` disabled (no `pages/` directory, or `pages: false`).
- The application must bind untrusted input to `:to`.
- A victim must click the rendered link.

## Affected versions

`nuxt` `<4.6.0`, including all Nuxt 3 releases. Versions before `4.4.7` and `3.21.7` are also affected by GHSA-934w-87qh-qr26.

## Patches

Fixed in `nuxt@4.6.0`. Nuxt 3 reached end of life on 31 July 2026 and will not receive a fix.

Anchor `href` values are now checked for script-capable protocols wherever they are rendered, including the router used when `pages` is disabled. Protocol detection also moved to the platform `URL` parser, so a URL is classified the same way the browser will read it.

## Workarounds

Upgrade to `nuxt@4.6.0` or later. If you cannot upgrade, including on Nuxt 3, validate values before binding them to `:to`, for example by rejecting anything that is not a path beginning with a single `/`.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

cves.summary:
### Summary

Nuxt compared `routeRules` keys against the raw request path, without decoding percent-encoding, while the router decodes parameters when it resolves a route. A request whose path is percent-encoded can therefore resolve to a page while failing to match the route rule meant to protect it, so the rule's `appMiddleware` never runs, including during server rendering.

### Impact

For a page served through a dynamic or catch-all route, an attacker can percent-encode a character in the path to skip the rule:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  routeRules: {
    '/users/admin': { appMiddleware: 'auth' },
  },
})
```

Requesting `/users/%61dmin` still renders `app/pages/users/[id].vue` with `id` decoded to `admin`, but the rule keyed `/users/admin` does not match, so `auth` does not run and the server renders and returns the gated page to an unauthenticated visitor. No privileges and no user interaction are required, and only ASCII characters are involved.

Purely static ASCII routes are not affected: static segments are matched without decoding, so a request for `/%61dmin` does not resolve to the page registered at `/admin` and 404s instead of rendering.

The rule keys affected are the ones carried in the app manifest and consumed by the app: `appMiddleware`, `redirect`, `appLayout`, `ssr`, `prerender`, and the payload flags derived from `cache`, `isr` and `swr`.

If you have pinned or overridden dependency versions below what your Nuxt release declares, a release outside the affected ranges can still be exposed, so do not conclude from a single reproduction that you are unaffected.

### Patches

Releases from `4.4.4` and `3.21.4` are not affected, because their dependency floor requires a version of the underlying HTTP layer that normalises percent-encoding in the request path before routing, which removes the mismatch in a default install.

The comparison itself is fixed in `nuxt@4.5.2` and `nuxt@3.21.11`: route-rule keys and lookup paths are now decoded (and, unless `router.options.sensitive` is set, case-folded) before they are compared. Reserved escapes such as `%2F` are left encoded, so decoding cannot introduce extra path segments, and paths that cannot be decoded are matched verbatim. Upgrading to those releases is recommended, since it fixes the comparison rather than relying on a dependency to normalise the input, and it also restores route rules for pages whose paths contain non-ASCII characters.

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade, do not rely on a `routeRules` key alone to protect a route. Attach the middleware to the page itself, which binds it to the resolved route rather than to the raw path string:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
definePageMeta({ middleware: 'auth' })
</script>
```

### Credits

Thanks to @sushi-gif, whose report that route rules keyed with non-ASCII paths never match the routes generated for those pages prompted the review that found this issue.

### Impact

An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large memory usage and/or long runtimes. This requires retrieving the form fields of a document.

### Patches

This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.0](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.0).

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4219](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4219).

### Summary

An attacker sending an absolute-form request can spoof the scheme used.

### Impact

If user code depends on the `Request.scheme` attribute for anything security related, an attacker may be able to circumvent this logic, tricking the application into thinking a connection is encrypted when it is not, or vice versa.

### Workaround

A WAF rule to reject absolute-form requests (legitimate requests should only use this form for proxies).

cwe.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

cves.summary:
### Summary

A subdomain can remove the Host-Only flag from an existing cookie to a parent domain.

### Impact

A user accessing untrusted subdomains could see their Host-Only protections stripped from cookies. Given most usecases won't reflect these cookies to a browser, the impact is limited.

cwe.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

cves.summary:
### Summary

An overflow in Max-Age processing can skip closing a connection.

### Impact

An attacker may be able to exhaust the connection pool temporarily, until garbage collection resolves the connections.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

cves.summary:
### Summary

The pure Python parser is vulnerable to an HTTP request smuggling attack.

### Impact

If users are using the Python parser (`AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS`, or not a standard wheel installed), then an application may be vulnerable to a request smuggling attack.

### Workaround

Switch to the default C parser.

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

cves.summary:
### Summary

An attacker can exhaust file descriptors with specially crafted multipart requests.

### Impact

If a handler uses `Request.post()`, it may be possible for an attacker to use an unlimited number of file descriptors, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion.

### Summary

`launch-editor` forwarded file paths directly to editors without sanitization. If a path resembles a CLI flag, editors like Vim may interpret it as a command, potentially causing unintended file overwrites or command execution.

### Impact

#### Direct `launch-editor` users

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- The first argument of `launchEditor` can start with `+` or `-` or the user is using WSL

#### `launch-editor-middleware` users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- launch-editor older than v2.2.0 is used, or the user is using WSL

#### Vite users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- The user is using WSL

### Details

`launchEditor(file)` function passes the file name as-is to the editor if the file with that file name exists. If the file name starts with `-` (also `+` for Vim), the editor treats them as flags rather than positional arguments. For example, Vim treats arguments starting with `+` as an Ex command. As a result, an existing relative directory such as:
```
+call writefile(["SAFE_MARKER"],"LAUNCH_EDITOR_MARKER")|qa!
```
is not treated as a filename when passed to Vim. Vim executes the embedded Ex command.

The following editor has a potentially destructive operation exposed to the CLI arguments:
- Vim (including gVim)
- MacVim
- Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)

`launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ converts the passed file path to an absolute path so those are not affected as long as the user is not using WSL. For WSL, `launch-editor` converts the paths to relative paths internally, so those are still affected.

Vite 2.0.0+ uses `launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ so the WSL users are only affected.

cves.summary: Lotus Domino HTTP server does not properly disable anonymous access for the cgi-bin directory.
Buffer overflow in Lotus Domino HTTP server allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long URL.

IIS does not properly canonicalize URLs, potentially allowing remote attackers to bypass access restrictions in third-party software via escape characters, aka the "Escape Character Parsing" vulnerability.

IIS 4.0 and Site Server 3.0 allow remote attackers to read source code for ASP files if the file is in a virtual directory whose name includes extensions such as .com, .exe, .sh, .cgi, or .dll, aka the "Virtual Directory Naming" vulnerability.

Internet Explorer 6.x on Windows XP SP2 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, as demonstrated using a document with a draggable file type such as .xml, .doc, .py, .cdf, .css, .pdf, or .ppt, and using ADODB.Connection and ADODB.recordset to write to a .hta file that is interpreted in the Local Zone by HTML Help.

## Summary YOURLS versions ≤1.10.4 contain an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to include and execute arbitrary PHP files on the server without any credentials. ## Details The vulnerability exists because YOURLS uses **URL sanitization functions** (`yourls_sanitize_url()`, `yourls_esc_url()`) to filter request paths, but these functions are designed to clean URLs, not filesystem paths. They preserve `/` and `.` characters, allowing `../` sequences to pass through unfiltered. The unsanitized keyword is then directly concatenated into a filesystem path and passed to `file_exists()` and later `include()` operations, enabling path traversal attacks. **Data Flow:** ``` HTTP Request URI (with ../) ↓ yourls_get_request() (no sanitization) ↓ yourls_sanitize_url() (preserves / and .) ↓ yourls_esc_url() (permits / and . via regex) ↓ Keyword extraction (preserves ../) ↓ file_exists(YOURLS_PAGEDIR . "/$keyword.php") ← Sink ↓ include(YOURLS_PAGEDIR . "/$keyword.php") ← Code Execution ``` ## Proof of Concept (POC) In the concept validation, we assume that the attacker has uploaded a `test.php` file to the web root directory, but it cannot be accessed directly. (Of course, it could also be any path, such as `/tmp/test.php`) ### Setup Place a test file in web root: `./test.php`: ```php ``` ### Attack Request ```http GET /../../test HTTP/1.1 Host: target.com Connection: close ``` ### Response (Apache Environment) ## Impact 1. Remote execution of uploaded PHP files – An attacker uploads a malicious PHP file to an arbitrary location on the server (e.g., via another vulnerability or file upload feature), obtains its absolute path but cannot access it directly. The attacker then leverages this vulnerability to include and execute the PHP file, gaining code execution privileges. 2. Indirect triggering of PHP code injection – If a PHP code injection point exists on the system (e.g., log injection, session injection) but the injected file cannot be accessed directly due to configuration restrictions, the attacker can use this vulnerability to include and execute the injected code, achieving remote command execution or further compromise.

cwe.name: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion')

cves.summary: Vulnerability in IntraGnat before 1.4.
netscript before 1.6.3 parses dynamic variables, which could allow remote attackers to alter program behavior or obtain sensitive information.
Cisco IOS 12.0 and other versions can be crashed by malicious UDP packets to the syslog port.

The URL pattern matching feature in BEA WebLogic Server 6.x matches illegal patterns ending in "*" as wildcards as if they were the legal "/*" pattern, which could cause WebLogic 7.x to allow remote attackers to bypass intended access restrictions because the illegal patterns are properly rejected.
